classification_rule: Every finding is CONFIRMED VULNERABILITY, SPEC CONFLICT, UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION or INCOMPLETE TESTING. A tool that cannot analyse a contract or times out is INCOMPLETE TESTING, not evidence of safety.

findings.rig: 7 (manual triage next to Slither, confirmed by PoC)
findings.damage_potential: Unbounded reward VCLM minted to stakers, up to the VCLM hard cap, from one real lock. The same gap can also be used to inflate an epoch basis past remaining capacity so honest stakers get nothing.
findings.description: racIdentity is supplied by the caller of the permissionless recordFeeAndRac and is not bound to the lock, transaction, log index or fee. One real lock can be recorded many times under different racIdentity values; each adds a full RAC credit to epochRewardBasis, which Stake.allocateEpoch later mints against. The app derives racIdentity from (env, lockId, txhash, logIndex, asset, fee) but the contract does not enforce it.
findings.evidence: PoC STATIC-C01: 5 racIdentity values for one lock, one credit 30e18, basis reached 150e18. PoC STATIC-C01b: 20 duplicate RACs for one 1000 USD lock; Stake minted 6000 VCLM for the epoch against an honest 300 VCLM (20x). testing-rigs/static-poc/verifier_input_gaps.test.cjs (output in poc_output.txt)
findings.rev_conflict: Rev 6 VF-RAC-001 (RAC exact-once): exact-once is enforced per caller-chosen id, not per lock or fee event.
findings.classification_note: Reproduced by PoC; also breaks Rev 6 VF-RAC-001.

findings.damage_potential: Any minter can take the day-0 emission rate forever, up to 10x the floor rate (SMTChecker I4 shows day 0 is the maximum rate).
findings.description: verifyAndMint computes emission days from pkg.valuationTimestamp, which the caller chooses. It is never compared with the reader-proven creation time extCreated (createdAt), which is only used for the CHONX activation check. valuationTimestamp=0 (or any time before launch) returns day 0.
findings.evidence: PoC STATIC-H02: lock one year after launch, honest mint 106.25 VCLM, same lock with valuationTimestamp=0 mints 130.0 VCLM. testing-rigs/static-poc/verifier_input_gaps.test.cjs (output in poc_output.txt)
findings.rev_conflict: Rev 6 VF-ORC-011/013 (emission rate from the Valuation Timestamp, which is the source block time, not a caller value).
findings.classification_note: Reproduced by PoC; also breaks Rev 6 VF-ORC-011/013.

findings.damage_potential: Free option for the user: wait for a better scheduled price, then submit the first proof. Over-issuance scales with price moves during the wait.
findings.description: The scheduled price is bound to a lock on the first proof submission (_resolveVerifiedGrossUsd), not at lock creation.
findings.evidence: PoC STATIC-M01: price 1000 at lock creation, poster moves to 2000, first proof binds 2000. testing-rigs/static-poc/verifier_input_gaps.test.cjs (output in poc_output.txt)
findings.rev_conflict: Rev 6 VF-ORC-009/010 and the rule that existing locks keep their creation price.
findings.classification_note: Reproduced by PoC; also breaks Rev 6 VF-ORC-009/010.

findings.damage_potential: If the poster key is lost, prices stop and all valuation stops. If it is compromised, any price can be posted (no bound or deviation check), which drives issuance directly.
findings.description: scheduledPricePoster is a single address. applyScheduledPriceRun accepts any positive price with no bounds, deviation limit or staleness rule. This is a trust assumption, rated low because the poster is an operator role by design.
findings.evidence: Code review: only checks are msg.sender == poster, runId increases, asset is registered, price > 0.
findings.classification_note: Safety rests on the single poster key posting correct prices; nothing on chain checks it.

findings.damage_potential: Fees for an environment with no Dev Fund destination are not caught at verify time.
findings.description: Step 10 Dev Fund destination check (VF-FEE-009) is commented out with a note that it is skipped in simulation.
findings.rev_conflict: Rev 6 VF-FEE-009 (check is required in production).
findings.classification_note: Rev 6 VF-FEE-009 requires the Dev Fund destination check; the code has it commented out.

findings.damage_potential: Griefing: a watcher can take a pending lockId first so the victim's lock call reverts. No funds lost.
findings.description: lockId is chosen by the caller and must be unused; a front-runner can use it first.
findings.classification_note: Assumes nobody front-runs a chosen lockId. Not reproduced in a PoC.

findings.damage_potential: A token that rebases down after deposit leaves the CVL short at release.
findings.description: The CVL measures the received amount by balance delta (good for fee-on-transfer tokens) but stores a fixed amount. A negative rebase later makes the stored amount larger than the balance. Rated low because the asset list is allowlisted.
findings.classification_note: Assumes no rebasing token is ever on the asset list.

findings.damage_potential: None today with the allowlisted tokens; would matter if a hook token were ever added.
findings.description: verifyAndMint and the Synth forge path write state after external calls (CEI not followed). Calls go to trusted tokens and readers, so the Slither entries are triaged FP for exploitability; kept here as a hardening note.
findings.classification_note: Safe only while every called token and reader is trusted and non-reentrant.

findings.damage_potential: One reverting or gas-heavy external call in a loop blocks the whole call.
findings.description: External calls inside loops. Targets are protocol contracts, so the risk is liveness only.
findings.classification_note: Assumes loop targets are protocol contracts that never revert or run out of gas.

findings.damage_potential: None. Callers may think daysSinceLaunch affects the mint.
findings.description: The daysSinceLaunch parameter of verifyAndMint is ignored.
findings.classification_note: Assumes no caller or off-chain tool relies on the ignored daysSinceLaunch value.

findings.damage_potential: A lock can be made with a false USD claim; the Verifier prices it again, so the effect is a lock that later fails to mint.
findings.description: The CVL Handshake and standard USD band gate uses verifiedGrossUsd as passed by the caller.
findings.rev_conflict: none found (Rev 12 band is re-checked by the Verifier on the priced value)
findings.classification_note: The CVL trusts the caller-supplied USD value; safety rests on the Verifier re-check of the Rev 12 band.

findings.description: extCreated from _verifySource is not used to bind valuationTimestamp.
findings.classification_note: Same root as STATIC-H02; Rev 6 VF-ORC-011/013 says the valuation time is the source block time.

findings.damage: none; the call reverts with Panic 0x11
findings.description: CHC found a real overflow trace in forge() for a huge count. Solidity 0.8 checked math turns it into a revert, so no wrap and no free mint.
findings.classification_note: Reverts, no damage. Assumes callers never need counts that large.

findings.description: CHC overflow trace for gross * STANDARD_FEE_BPS when gross > 2^256/500. Checked math reverts. No real token has that supply. Same trace on the extracted copy (FeeMath.sol:37).
findings.classification_note: Reverts, no damage. Assumes no listed token has a supply above 2^256/500.

findings.damage: none; reverts, the lock fails closed
findings.description: CHC underflow trace for _balanceOf(after) - beforeBal when the pulled token lowers the vault balance during transferFrom (a hostile or rebasing token). Checked math reverts, so the lock is refused. Ties to finding L04 (rebasing tokens).
findings.classification_note: Reverts (fails closed). Assumes listed tokens do not lower the vault balance on transferFrom.

findings.description: CHC overflow trace for createdAt + duration. duration is limited to the fixed CommitmentDurations table, so only a solver-chosen huge timestamp reaches it. Checked math reverts.
findings.classification_note: Reverts, no damage. Assumes sane block timestamps.

findings.file_line: base-contracts/contracts/VinculumFinalisToken.sol:122 (hardCap set at :84 with no range check)
findings.description: CHC overflow trace for totalSupply + amount. It needs a deployment with hardCap near 2^256, which the constructor accepts without a check. Checked math reverts. Deployment script must pass the Rev 6 cap.
findings.classification_note: Reverts, no damage. Assumes the deployment passes the Rev 6 hard cap; the constructor does not check it.

smtchecker.formal_layer: solc 0.8.19 SMTChecker, CHC engine, z3 4.11.2. Certora not available (CERTORAKEY not set in env), so SMTChecker is the only formal layer.
smtchecker.note_checked_math: Solidity 0.8 checked arithmetic: an overflow or underflow 'happens' result means the call reverts with Panic 0x11, not a silent wrap.
notes: prod_synth (production VinculumFinalisSynth.sol): FAIL-TO-RUN. solc/libz3 crashes with SIGSEGV after about 25 s, three times, with a 5 GB cap, a 6.5 GB cap and no cap. The Synth properties are covered by the instrumented copy (harness_synth), which ran to completion.
prod_stake and prod_verifier ran to exit 0 but almost every target came back 'Error trying to invoke SMT solver' (92 of 97 and 49 of 56). Those targets are inconclusive, not proven.

harness_feemath first run inherited the whole BaseCommitmentVaultLock and was OOM-killed (exit 247). It was replaced by FeeMath.sol, a verbatim extract of _quote (extract_feemath.py), which ran in 26 s.
A second token run with only the assert target was OOM-killed after 639 s (results/harness_token_assert_only.txt).
The box rebooted about 07:18 EDT on Oct 23 and /workspace was restored from a snapshot. prod_verifier and prod_synth were rerun after that; all other outputs survived.
Supplementary BMC runs (run_bmc_supplement.sh) are labelled as such and are not counted as CHC verdicts.
